intro: Wet room installation is one of the most transformative bathroom upgrades you can make, and it's becoming increasingly popular across Borthwicklee as homeowners look to modernise their spaces without compromising on practicality. Whether you're planning ahead for later-life accessibility, simply want a sleek, open showering space, or are upgrading a tired bathroom that's seen better days, a properly installed wet room adds real value and daily comfort. In a small community like Borthwicklee, where homes range from characterful stone cottages to newer modern builds, getting the installation right from the outset is everything — poor waterproofing or inadequate drainage can cause serious damage that's costly to fix.
localContext: Borthwicklee sits in Midlothian's rolling countryside, and the housing stock here reflects that rural Scottish character well. You'll find older stone-built properties and period cottages where original bathroom layouts are often compact, with solid stone walls that need careful preparation before any wet room work begins. Tanking these surfaces correctly is non-negotiable — stone walls absorb moisture differently from modern plasterboard, and a contractor unfamiliar with older construction can easily underestimate the prep work involved. Borthwicklee's modern estate homes present a more straightforward canvas, but still require attention to subfloor integrity and correct fall gradients for drainage. It's also worth noting that Borthwicklee sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale build-up on shower screens, fittings, and drains is a genuine consideration. Choosing fittings with scale-resistant coatings and planning for easy drain access will save you maintenance headaches down the line.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Borthwicklee typically follows a clear sequence of work, and understanding the process helps you plan realistically. The job begins with a full strip-out of the existing bathroom — removing tiles, sanitaryware, flooring, and any damaged plasterwork. In older stone-built properties and period cottages, this stage can reveal surprises: uneven subfloors, historic pipework, or walls that need repointing before waterproofing can begin. Once stripped, the installer assesses the subfloor and builds up a tanking system — a fully waterproof membrane that covers floors and walls to a minimum height, usually 1.8 metres. This is the most critical stage of the whole job, and cutting corners here is where wet rooms fail. The floor is then graded to direct water toward a linear or central drain, which requires precise screeding work. In Borthwicklee homes with solid stone floors or uneven original joists, this can add time and cost to achieve the correct fall. Tiling follows once the screed has fully cured — typically 48 to 72 hours. Your chosen tiles, shower fixtures, and glass screens or panels are then fitted, followed by final plumbing connections and a thorough leak test before the room is signed off. From start to finish, most installations take five to eight working days.
pricing: In Borthwicklee, wet room installations typically run between £6,500 and £12,000, depending on the scope of work and the property type involved. Older stone-built properties and period cottages tend to sit toward the higher end of that range due to additional prep work, more complex tanking requirements, and the likelihood of unforeseen structural discoveries. Modern estate homes with standard timber-frame construction are generally more straightforward, keeping costs closer to the lower end. The size of the room, your choice of tiles and fixtures, and whether you're moving any pipework or drainage all influence the final figure significantly. VAT is included in these estimates for most residential customers.
whyLocal: In a small place like Borthwicklee, word travels fast — which means local tradespeople have a strong incentive to do the job properly. Someone who knows the area will understand the particular quirks of Midlothian stone-built properties, the local climate's effect on older structures, and how to work efficiently within the constraints of a rural location where supply runs to Edinburgh or Dalkeith add time to the job. A local installer is also far easier to contact if a snag arises after completion, and that ongoing relationship matters when you've invested upward of £6,000 in your home.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwicklee?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than a modern home. Stone walls need thorough assessment before tanking, and solid floors may need build-up work to achieve the correct drainage gradient. An experienced installer will factor this in from the survey stage rather than discovering it mid-job. Always get a quote that explicitly covers older property preparation.

faqs.q: Will hard water in Borthwicklee affect my wet room long-term?
faqs.a: Moderately hard water does mean limescale will gradually build up on fittings, drains, and any glass screens. It's not a dealbreaker, but it's worth choosing fittings with anti-scale coatings and ensuring your drain cover is easy to remove for regular cleaning. A water softener isn't essential, but some Borthwicklee homeowners do install one for whole-house benefit.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwicklee?
faqs.a: Most installations take between five and eight working days from strip-out to completion. Older properties with stone walls or uneven floors can push that closer to ten days if additional preparation is needed. Your installer should give you a realistic timeline after the initial survey, not before — any quote given without a site visit should be treated with caution.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a property in Borthwicklee?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly if it replaces an outdated bathroom in a period cottage or older stone-built home. A well-executed wet room signals quality and modern standards to buyers, and the accessibility angle is increasingly valued. In a small community like Borthwicklee where property turnover is low, the day-to-day quality of life benefit is often just as important as the resale consideration.
